diagnoses.description: silence-detector computes the end timestamp of initial silence incorrectly because the smoothing convolution uses mode='valid' but the returned index is treated as if it were aligned to the original per-second energy timeline. This produces a systematic time shift (roughly half the smoothing window, or up to smoothing_window-1 seconds depending on interpretation), causing downstream pause detection to start too early/late and video cuts to be misaligned.
diagnoses.evidence: In silence-detector/scripts/detect_silence.py, smoothed energies are computed with np.convolve(..., mode='valid'), which shortens the array by smoothing_window-1. The loop index i is then assigned directly to silence_end and used as seconds in the original timeline. With a 30s smoothing window, i=0 corresponds to original time ~0..29, not second 0. This mismatch matches the hint about smoothing window and timestamps correspondence.

locations.section: detect_initial_silence(): smoothing via np.convolve(..., mode='valid') and silence_end assignment
How It Works / Notes: lacks explicit statement of timestamp alignment and smoothing behavior

diagnoses.description: video-processor/SKILL.md instructs starting pause detection at the silence detector boundary, but does not warn that the boundary must be in the same time base as the energy windows (window_seconds) and must be corrected for smoothing alignment. This can lead to agents passing a misaligned start-time into pause-detector, compounding the cut errors.
diagnoses.evidence: video-processor/SKILL.md step 3 says to 'start long-pause detection at that returned boundary' but does not specify that silence-detector returns seconds aligned to energy window centers/starts, nor does it mention smoothing-window offset. Given the current silence-detector implementation, the returned boundary is ambiguous and likely wrong; the doc should make the contract explicit so callers can rely on it.

diagnoses.description: silence-detector returns only an integer second boundary without clarifying whether it is inclusive/exclusive and whether it refers to the start of the first non-silent window or the end of the last silent window. This ambiguity can cause off-by-one errors when converting to removal segments and when using the boundary as pause-detector --start-time.
diagnoses.evidence: detect_silence.py sets segment {start:0,end:silence_end,duration:silence_end}. pause-detector treats start-time as an index into energies (seconds). Without a defined convention (e.g., end is exclusive), callers may remove one extra second or leave one silent second. The docs do not define this precisely.

locations.section: Output Format / Notes: missing explicit timebase and exclusivity convention
main(): building segments with end=silence_end and duration=silence_end

quality_impact.rationale: Fixes a concrete timestamp misalignment bug that would directly cause wrong opening boundary and downstream mis-cuts. Uses centered smoothing with same-length output, eliminating the 'valid' convolution shift. Adds explicit timebase/interval semantics to reduce off-by-one and unit confusion.

trigger_precision.rationale: Targets the silence-detector smoothing/timestamp contract and the video-processor documentation that depends on it, matching the hint. The change is general (any energy window size, any smoothing window) and not tuned to a specific video.

instruction_compliance.rationale: Attributes the defect to Skill code/doc mismatch rather than agent behavior, and makes the required checks/actions explicit via a clarified contract (energy index timebase, half-open intervals). Does not introduce task-instance steps or outputs.

solution_path_coverage.rationale: Handles edge cases: empty energies, very short audio, smoothing_window<=1, initial_window bounds. Provides stable alignment for both odd/even smoothing windows and documents how callers should pass the boundary to pause-detector.

skillaxe_evaluation.overall_rationale: The bundle’s main failure mode is misaligned timestamps from smoothing in silence-detector, which propagates into incorrect pause detection start times and segment removal boundaries. The repair corrects the algorithmic alignment and updates documentation at the integration boundary to prevent recurrence across tasks.
